trials.notes: Passed all cases with documented calls. Slight processor-choice penalty: it used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() even though the docs recommend the lighter WP_HTML_Tag_Processor for flat template filling and byte-preserving attribute/text edits. The actual mutation pattern was idiomatic: template attributes, placeholder text, token walk to #text, set_attribute(), set_modifiable_text(), get_updated_html().

Matches the documented Tag Processor template-building recipe and the canonical approach. It uses the correct processor, preserves attribute order by predeclaring attributes, writes plain unescaped strings through set_attribute() and set_modifiable_text(), and returns get_updated_html().
Same strong adherence as trial-2. No undocumented API usage, no _doing_it_wrong records, and the implementation follows the rendered docs' template-building pattern exactly.

failure_analysis: All trials passed all hidden cases, including ampersands, quotes, angle brackets, Unicode, and caption text that looks like HTML. The docs did well because the Tag Processor page has a directly relevant 'Building markup from a template' section: include attributes in the template to preserve order, include placeholder text so there is a #text token to replace, use set_attribute() and set_modifiable_text() with plain unescaped values, then read output with get_updated_html(). The set_attribute() and set_modifiable_text() docs also explicitly explain that these methods perform HTML encoding, which prevented double-escaping and injection-style failures. The only near-miss was trial-1 choosing HTML Processor because the task says 'fragment'; that still worked and was documented, but it was heavier than necessary for a fixed flat template.

doc_gaps.location: html-processor.md Method Index / inherited Tag Processor APIs
doc_gaps.problem: The page references inherited mutation output APIs such as get_updated_html() in prose, but not all inherited callable methods used for mutation are surfaced consistently in the method index or as short inherited-method sections.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add an 'Inherited Tag Processor mutation APIs' table or entries for set_modifiable_text() and get_updated_html(), each pointing back to the Tag Processor docs and clarifying they are callable on WP_HTML_Processor instances.

doc_gaps.problem: A reader may choose HTML Processor merely because they are producing or processing an HTML fragment, even when no parsed structure, breadcrumbs, implied tags, or normalized serialization are needed.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short decision note under create_fragment(): use HTML Processor when fragment parsing/tree semantics matter; for fixed templates with attribute/text replacement, prefer WP_HTML_Tag_Processor.

doc_gaps.problem: The prose says to always check the return value, while nearby template-style examples rely on first matching a #text token and do not show a check. This is mostly fine, but the contract around when failure is still possible is implicit.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Clarify which token types are expected to accept arbitrary plain text, when set_modifiable_text() can still return false, and either check the return value in examples or explicitly note why the controlled #text-template case omits fallback handling.
